abstractExcerpt: Kinetic models for Fe2O3 reduction by hydrogen determine fuel-reactor volume, solid inventory, and achievable hydrogen yield in chemical-looping hydrogen generation (CLHG) reactors. Conventional thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) workflows require an a priori choice of reaction model—shrinking-core, grain, or Johnson–Mehl–Avrami—before Arrhenius parameters can be fitted, and that assumption is restrictive when particle morphology or transport regime is uncertain.

title: CALISTO: A Standardized and Open-Source Software for Magnetic Tweezer Force Calibration

s2.tldr: CALISTO provides an open-source, standardized framework that integrates force calibration with automated quality control and quantitative assessment of experimental data and provides a practical foundation for more reliable quantitative single-molecule force measurements.

abstractExcerpt: Magnetic tweezers (MT) enable multiplexed single-molecule force spectroscopy while applying controlled forces and torques to biomolecules. They resolve forces below 1 pN and maintain constant forces over extended periods, but accurate calibration remains challenging due to drift, tracking artifacts, camera noise, and bead variability. Here, we present CALISTO (CALIbration Suite for magnetic Tweezer Operation), an open-source software for MT force calibration. CALISTO analyzes position traces of DNA-tethered magnetic beads and surface-bound reference beads for drift correction.

title: Decoding enzyme-substrate interaction topology reveals principles underlying catalytic efficiency and mutational outcomes

s2.tldr: Interkcat is developed, an interpretable bidirectional cross-attention framework that captures reciprocal coordination between protein residues and substrate atoms that establishes interaction topology as a unifying principle linking enzyme sequence, catalytic efficiency, and evolutionary perturbation.

abstractExcerpt: The enzyme turnover number (kcat) defines catalytic efficiency and constrains quantitative models of metabolism, yet the molecular determinants governing kcat and its response to mutation remain poorly understood. Measurements are sparse and labor-intensive, and most computational approaches provide numerical predictions without explaining how enzyme-substrate interactions shape catalytic outcomes.

Gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) hydrogels have emerged as versatile biomaterials for biomedical engineering because of their biocompatibility, extracellular matrix-like structure, tunable mechanical properties, photocrosslinkability, and capacity to incorporate therapeutic agents, imaging probes, and functional nanomaterials.

Model usefulness must be defined relative to a specific question and validated against independent experimental observables.
